datasets.name: GEF Mumbai 2027 (simulated plan)
datasets.description: Simulated data for the Global Entrepreneurship Fest, Mumbai, built from our deck plan and the GES playbook. Fictional companies and people.
datasets.prob_source: GES playbook funnel (100 called -> 10 good leads -> 5 meetings -> 1 signed): prospect 1%, good lead 10%, meeting 20%. Assumptions [A]: not connected yet 0.3%, connected or proposal mailed without a reply yet 0.5%, follow-up with no reply 0.3%, negotiation 50%.

campaigns.name: Base engine: sector outreach
campaigns.objective: Call every qualified company in each member's sector group, email the proposal, follow up

campaigns.name: IT + AI sweep
campaigns.objective: Sweep IT firms that fests rarely approach, plus AI firms launching to students
campaigns.audience: 1,000+ IT firms and AI product companies

campaigns.name: Active sponsors
campaigns.objective: Companies that sponsored fests or events this year or last
campaigns.test: 8+ good leads from the first 50 contacted

rule.change_action: Re-order the list by recency and switch contacts

campaigns.name: Conglomerates (business units)
campaigns.objective: Pitch business units of 5 to 6 large groups one by one
campaigns.test: 3+ meetings from the first 30 business units

rule.change_action: Reach the units through speaker invites

campaigns.name: Event titles
campaigns.objective: Sell the title of one event (MAS, Investor Startup Connect) to a targeted group

rule.change_action: Offer the title inside a regular package

campaigns.name: Government + CSR
campaigns.objective: CSR arms, state tourism boards, PSUs; states split across members
campaigns.test: 2+ conversations by week 4 and 1 proposal in sanction by week 6

rule.stop_action: No new entities, keep warm ones

campaigns.name: Mass email
campaigns.objective: Timed email bursts growing toward the fest

targets.note: Deck base case: 10 deals + CSR, Rs 26L signed, Rs 12.1L to 13.8L before fest
Deck stretch: ~18 to 20 deals, Rs 33.7L to 40.3L signed, Rs 15.7L to 21.5L before fest

notes.title: 4 guests visiting for the fest
notes.detail: 4 people from their team attend on 30 and 31 Jan. Book guest-house rooms for 2 nights and arrange airport pickup on 29 Jan evening.
notes.brief: 4 guests on 30-31 Jan: rooms + pickup needed

notes.title: GST invoice needed before advance
notes.detail: Their finance team releases the advance only against a GST invoice addressed to the Mumbai office. Send it with the agreement.
notes.brief: Needs GST invoice before paying the advance

notes.title: Logo on participant kits
notes.detail: They want their logo on all participant kits. Share the kit design for approval by 15 Jan.

notes.title: CEO may judge MAS
notes.detail: Their CEO is open to judging MAS (Million At Stake). Confirm the slot and travel by 10 Jan.
notes.brief: CEO may judge MAS: confirm by 10 Jan

notes.title: Meeting with Meridian Tyres
notes.detail: Interested in the Strategic package; wants footfall proof and last year's branding report. Decision expected by 5 Dec. Next: send the GES branding report and a revised deck by Monday.
notes.brief: Meridian Tyres: Interested in Strategic; decision by 5 Dec

notes.title: Meeting with Indus Labs
notes.detail: Marketing head liked the workshop idea. Budget is approved only for Q4; they asked to hold the price till 10 Dec. Next: send the workshop outline and hold the slab.
notes.brief: Indus Labs: Likes the workshop idea; price hold till 10 Dec

notes.title: Meeting with Juniper Systems
notes.detail: They sponsor another Mumbai fest in January. Pitched category exclusivity (+Rs 50K). They will reply after their internal review on 3 Dec.
notes.brief: Juniper Systems: Sponsors another fest; pitched exclusivity

notes.title: Meeting with Arunodaya Group - Retail
notes.detail: Group CMO prefers one combined deal across business units. Do not pitch the other units separately until the CMO replies.
notes.brief: Arunodaya Group - Retail: Group wants one combined deal: do not pitch other units separately

notes.title: Meeting with Delta Consulting
notes.detail: Asked for a stall plus 2 speaker passes instead of a panel slot. Negotiating Corporate at Rs 1.5L with 2 passes.
notes.brief: Delta Consulting: Negotiating Corporate with 2 speaker passes

notes.title: Meeting with Ridge Pay Pvt Ltd
notes.detail: Needs approval from their Delhi office. Contact shared the approver's email; follow up with them directly.
notes.brief: Ridge Pay Pvt Ltd: Approval sits with Delhi office; follow up there

sequences.name: GES follow-up (3 weeks)
sequences.description: Our playbook after the first call: proposal email, then a follow-up email every other day and a call twice a week. No reply in 3 weeks: switch to another contact. Any reply stops the sequence and goes to the owner to handle by hand.

steps.subject: Sponsorship proposal: {{fest}} x {{company}}
steps.body:
Hi {{first_name}},

Thank you for taking my call today. As promised, I have attached our sponsorship proposal for {{fest}}.

The fest draws 20,000 to 25,000+ footfall, with 120K+ social reach and a million+ media impressions. Partners get stage branding, speaker slots, stalls and direct access to students.

The {{package}} package could fit {{company}} well. Would you have 20 minutes this week to discuss it?

Best regards,
{{sender}}
Corporate & Media Relations, {{fest}}

steps.subject: Re: Sponsorship proposal: {{fest}} x {{company}}
steps.body:
Hi {{first_name}},

Just checking that the proposal reached you. Happy to walk you through it on a quick call or adjust the package to what {{company}} wants to achieve.

Best,
{{sender}}

steps.subject: Follow-up call
steps.body: Ask if they saw the proposal; find the decision maker and their timeline.

steps.subject: {{company}} at {{fest}}: a few ideas
steps.body:
Hi {{first_name}},

A few ways partners like {{company}} have used the fest: a hands-on workshop for students, a speaker slot in a panel, or category exclusivity on the main stage.

If any of these is interesting, I can share a short plan.

Best,
{{sender}}

steps.subject: Reach and footfall from our last edition
steps.body:
Hi {{first_name}},

Sharing last edition's numbers: 20,000 to 25,000+ footfall, 120K+ social reach and 20+ media partners. Happy to send the branding report from last year as well.

Best,
{{sender}}

steps.subject: Partner slots for {{fest}}
steps.body:
Hi {{first_name}},

We are finalising partners for {{fest}} over the next few weeks. Would it help if I held the {{package}} slot for {{company}} while you review?

Best,
{{sender}}

steps.subject: Follow-up call
steps.body: Ask about budget timing and who signs off.

steps.subject: Would a short call help?
steps.body:
Hi {{first_name}},

I know inboxes get busy. If a 15-minute call is easier than email, just reply with a time that suits you.

Best,
{{sender}}

steps.subject: Follow-up call
steps.body: Last call attempt with this contact this week.

steps.subject: Last note from the {{fest}} team
steps.body:
Hi {{first_name}},

I will not keep filling your inbox. If someone else at {{company}} handles partnerships or brand events, could you point me to them?

Thank you,
{{sender}}

steps.subject: Final call
steps.body: Ask for the right person; if no answer, prepare to switch contact on day 21.
